# The PR-body lint gate exists in no repo, and the skill still names it

## Context

`pull-request-workflow.md` §9 — the skill every agent loads before opening a PR — makes this promise, verbatim at line 337:

> `agent-pr-body-lint.yml` enforces `Evidence:`, `## AC Evidence`, `## Test Evidence`, `## Post-Merge Validation`, `## Deltas`, `Authored by ` as **unconditional** anchors — presence is never prose-conditional (PR #14465). The AC-Evidence CONTENT is machine-checked too: the lint resolves the close target and fails a certificate that misses the ticket's AC count or leaves a proof slot empty.

**That workflow exists in no repository.** It was deleted from this one on 2026-08-26 and was never re-homed. Every clause of that sentence — the filename, "unconditional", "machine-checked" — is currently false, and the seats reading it have no way to know.

Measured 2026-08-31, ~06:33Z:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/agent-pr-body-lint.yml` at Engine `dev` | **absent** |
| `git log --all -- <that path>` | last touched by `91ae3604b4` — a **deletion**, 253 lines, 14,809 B |
| that commit | `fix(engine): remove received Brain substrate (#17791)`, @tobiu, 2026-08-26 (also `c623b2f63c`, #17806) |
| `neo-agent-brain` `.github/workflows/` | 10 workflows, **none** is a PR-body lint |
| `neo-agent-skills` `.github/workflows/` | `reusable-pr-baseline.yml` (PR **base branch**), `skill-corpus.yml` — **neither** lints bodies |
| `validatePrBody` / `agent-preflight` anywhere in Engine source | **no hit**; the only residue is `docs/output/src/ai/scripts/agent-preflight.json`, a generated docs artifact for a script that left |

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-31T06:36:05Z; no equivalent found. A2A in-flight claim sweep over the last 30 messages immediately before filing: no `[lane-claim]`/`[lane-intent]` on this scope.

## The Problem

**A gate nobody notices is missing is worse than a gate that was never promised**, and this one is actively asserted by the substrate that replaces judgement.

The gate ran on `pull_request: [opened, edited, synchronize, ready_for_review]`, scoped to agent authors (`neo-` login prefix, or the `ai` label). It was load-bearing: the Memory Core records it going red and blocking work repeatedly across months — on my own PRs (#14344, #15424), on @neo-opus-ada's (#13393), on @neo-fable's (#12921) — each time naming the exact missing anchor. Seats learned the anchor set *from this gate failing them*.

It is not merely theoretically missing. **A PR carrying two missing unconditional anchors merged into `dev` today.**

> **Corrected 2026-08-31 06:56Z by me, the author.** This section first said #17902 was "sitting at the operator merge gate right now" and that I repaired its body. Both were wrong on the timeline: #17902 **merged at 06:31:27Z**, before I measured its anchors at ~06:33Z; my 06:34Z body edit amended an already-merged PR and prevented nothing. I had read it as open in a `gh pr list` at 06:29:44Z and never re-read live state before asserting — the stale-snapshot failure this repo has a rule against. The defect is worse than I first described, not better.

PR #17902 — APPROVED cross-family at Round 2, CLEAN, `gh pr checks` exit 0, `reviewRequests` empty — carried a body missing **two** unconditional anchors, `## AC Evidence` and `## Test Evidence`, and merged with them. Nothing caught it:

- **CI could not** — the gate is deleted.
- **The local preflight could not** — `npm run agent-preflight` is unrunnable outside the Brain (`neo-agent-skills#24`).
- **Two review rounds did not** — reviewers read for substance, and reasonably trust a mechanical gate to do the mechanical half.

That PR is mine, so this is a self-report, not a peer finding. I repaired its body at 06:34Z; **that repair fixes one artifact, not the hole.** The control matters too: PR #17912 and #17915 carry all six anchors, so the template is satisfiable and the rule is not broken — which is exactly what silent drift looks like. Some pass, some do not, and nothing distinguishes them.

`#17783`'s own history records the same cost at larger scale before the split: three PRs passed two human-equivalent review rounds while failing the body lint that was never run.

**The promise is the aggravating factor.** An agent that reads "unconditional" and "machine-checked" has been given a positive reason *not* to hand-verify. The substrate is not silent here; it is wrong, and it is wrong in the direction that suppresses the compensating behaviour.

## The Architectural Reality

The deleted workflow ran **three** steps, and the distinction between them is the whole of this ticket's prescription. Recoverable in full at `91ae3604b4^:.github/workflows/agent-pr-body-lint.yml`.

| step | implementation | Brain-dependent? |
|---|---|---|
| `Validate PR body with the owning implementation` | `node ai/scripts/agent-preflight.mjs --pr-body … --pr-base …` — the AC-Evidence **content** check | **yes** — `ai/scripts/` left with the split |
| `Validate PR Body` | inline `actions/github-script@v9`; `VISIBLE_PR_BODY_ANCHORS` + `INVISIBLE_PR_BODY_ANCHORS` substring checks and the `Resolves #N` regex (operator rule `#12367`) | **no — zero repository dependencies** |
| `Stacked-PR guard` | `node ./ai/scripts/lint/lint-pr-stacking.mjs` | **yes** — `ai/scripts/lint/` no longer exists here |

So the deletion was *correct as a mechanical act* — two of three steps invoked scripts that had left, and a workflow whose steps cannot run is not a gate. It was collateral, not a policy decision: #17791 is scoped to "removes exactly the cut-manifest mover set", and this workflow was swept along because it *called* mover-set scripts, not because PR-body enforcement was retired.

**The consequential fact: the anchor step is entirely self-contained.** It reads the PR body through the Actions API and tests substrings in inline JS. It needs no checkout, no `npm ci`, no Brain, no cross-repo caller decision. It can be restored today, alone, and it is precisely the step that would have caught #17902.

Two properties in the deleted file were paid for by earlier tickets and must survive any restore — a fresh re-author would silently drop both:

- **The body is fetched LIVE (`gh pr view`), never from `github.event.pull_request.body`.** That field is an event snapshot, which made the gate wrong in both directions: a corrected body could never go green (`gh run rerun` replays the original payload), and a body edited after a green run kept that green. This is `#17431`, closed COMPLETED — its fix lives only in the deleted file.
- **The body reaches the validator through a FILE, never `${{ }}` inside `run:`.** A PR body is attacker-controlled text; interpolating it into a shell splices it into the script. Deleting the file deleted the only place that property is written down.

Sibling precedent for placement is unambiguous and needs no novel directory: `.github/workflows/` already carries eight `*-lint.yml` workflows, including `agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml` — the **review**-body gate, which survived because its inline script has no Brain dependency. That file is the exact positive control for what this ticket restores.

## The Fix

Split by dependency, and land the free half first.

1. **Restore the dependency-free anchor gate** as `.github/workflows/agent-pr-body-lint.yml`, lifted from `91ae3604b4^` and reduced to the `Validate PR Body` `github-script` step plus its agent-author `if:` condition — carrying forward, verbatim and with their comments, the live-fetch property (#17431) and the file-not-shell-interpolation property. Drop the `Setup Node`/`npm ci`/checkout scaffolding the two removed steps needed.
2. **Correct the skill's promise to match what actually runs.** `pull-request-workflow.md:337` must stop asserting machine-checked AC-Evidence **content** while only anchor **presence** is enforced. This edit cannot be made from this repository — the corpus is a symlink into `node_modules/neo-agent-skills`, so it lands as a `neo-agent-skills` change and reaches seats only on release. Track under that repo; this ticket is not closed by it.
3. **Record the two orphaned halves rather than silently dropping them** — the `agent-preflight` content check and the stacked-PR guard both need a cross-repository caller, which is `neo-agent-skills#14`'s authority and `#24`'s mechanism. Out of scope here (below), named so they are not lost a second time.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.github/workflows/agent-pr-body-lint.yml`, job `lint-pr-body`, step `Validate PR Body` | This repository — the workflow gates this repository's PRs; sibling precedent `agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml` | On `opened`/`edited`/`synchronize`/`ready_for_review`, for `neo-`-prefixed authors or `ai`-labelled PRs, fail when the body omits any of `Evidence:`, `## AC Evidence`, `## Test Evidence`, `## Post-Merge Validation`, `## Deltas`, `Authored by `, or carries no `Resolves #N` | None — the fallback is today's state: zero enforcement under a skill that promises enforcement | `pull-request-workflow.md` §9 line 337, corrected to name only what runs | A body missing one anchor reds the check; the same body with the anchor added goes green on the `edited` event without a push |
| `pull-request-workflow.md:337` (`neo-agent-skills`) | `neo-agent-skills` — Engine cannot edit its own loaded corpus (symlink into `node_modules`) | States anchor **presence** is enforced by the named workflow; drops or re-scopes the machine-checked AC-Evidence **content** claim until a caller exists | Leaving it is the current defect — a false promise that suppresses hand-verification | the file itself | `grep` of the released corpus shows no claim without a running enforcer |

Row anchors verified before assertion: the workflow path, job name, step names, both anchor arrays and the `if:` condition were read at `91ae3604b4^`; the skill line was read through `readlink -f .agents/skills`.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. This restores an enforcement surface that was removed as collateral; it does not alter the split's dependency direction. Note for whoever picks it up: ADR 0040 (which governs the cut) is **not** in this repository's `learn/agentos/decisions/` — it moved with the Brain, so an Engine-local ADR sweep for it returns a false absence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/agent-pr-body-lint.yml` exists in this repository and runs on `pull_request` for agent-authored PRs, with no step depending on any script or package outside this repository.
- [ ] All six anchors and the `Resolves #N` requirement are enforced, matching the arrays at `91ae3604b4^`.
- [ ] The live-body-fetch property (#17431) is preserved: a body corrected after a red run goes green on the `edited` event, **without** a push. Demonstrated, not asserted.
- [ ] The PR body is never interpolated into a shell `run:` block; it reaches any consumer through a file.
- [ ] A negative control proves the gate can fail: a body with exactly one anchor removed reds the check, and restoring that anchor greens it. Presence of the workflow file is not evidence it enforces anything.
- [ ] The workflow carries a header comment stating which enforcement halves are **not** present (AC-Evidence content, stacked-PR guard) and where they are tracked, so the next reader does not re-derive that the gate is partial.
- [ ] Cross-repo, non-closing: a `neo-agent-skills` change corrects line 337 so no clause names an enforcer that is not running. This ticket does not gate on that release.

## Out of Scope

- **Re-homing the `agent-preflight` content check.** It is Brain-owned and needs a cross-repository caller — `neo-agent-skills#14` (caller authority) and `#24` (the mandate is unrunnable outside the Brain) own that. Restoring the anchor half must not wait on it.
- **The stacked-PR guard** (`lint-pr-stacking.mjs`). Same class, same blocker, separate disposition; `#16589` is its origin.
- **Making this a required status context on `dev`.** `#17171` owns that decision for all nineteen lint workflows; adding one more unrequired check does not change its shape.
- **Renegotiating the anchor set.** This restores the rules as they were. Any argument that six anchors is the wrong number is a separate ticket against `pull-request-workflow.md` §9.
- **The other post-split residuals.** `#17783` is deliberately narrowed to R2/R3 (authorship guard, hook↔CI parity) and is assigned; this is a distinct fifth residual, filed separately rather than grown onto someone else's scoped ticket.

## Avoided Traps

- **Re-authoring the workflow from the skill's prose instead of restoring the file.** The prose names the anchor list and nothing else. Re-authoring would silently drop the live-fetch fix (#17431, a closed COMPLETED ticket whose only surviving implementation is in the deleted blob) and the shell-injection property, reintroducing two solved defects. Lift from `91ae3604b4^`; do not retype.
- **Treating the deletion as a policy decision and closing this as WONTFIX.** #17791's scope is the cut-manifest mover set. The workflow was swept in because it *called* mover-set scripts, and the skill still mandates the rules — so the swarm's stated policy never changed. Deletion-by-collateral reads identical to deletion-by-decision in `git log`; the discriminator is the ticket scope and the still-live mandate.
- **Waiting for the cross-repo caller question to be settled.** The anchor step has no cross-repo dependency at all. Bundling it with the two Brain-dependent halves would park a free, complete fix behind an unsettled placement decision — which is how this became invisible for five days in the first place.
- **Declaring the file's absence from a `grep -r` of `.agents/`.** That directory is a symlink into `node_modules`, and `grep -r` does not follow symlinks — it reports a clean zero that reads exactly like an absence. Use `grep -R`, or `readlink -f` first. (`#24` records the same false negative on its first sweep.)
- **Calling `agent-pr-review-body-lint.yml` the same gate.** It is a different, surviving workflow that lints **review** bodies. A sweep matching on `pr.*body.*lint` finds it and concludes the gate is present.

## Superseded by `neomjs/neo-agent-skills#30` + `#29` — closing NOT_PLANNED

Third of three tonight (`#17911`, `#17913`, this one), all the same mistake: filing Engine-local restorations of governance that five-plus repositories need identically. @tobiu caught each of them, this one by title.

**The ticket's diagnosis was right and stays on the record.** §9 promised a gate (`agent-pr-body-lint.yml`) that existed in no repository after `91ae3604b4`, and the promise had a measured victim — PR #17902 merged into `dev` at 06:31:27Z missing `## AC Evidence` and `## Test Evidence`. What was wrong was the **address**, not the finding.

**Where it landed instead:**

- **`neo-agent-skills#30`** — the validator as a tested portable CLI (`scripts/check-pr-body.mjs` + a mutation-sensitive contract), which also closes `#28`: the old gate matched anchors as substrings, so a body that merely *discussed* an anchor satisfied it. `corpus` green at `7a87fe1`. **§9 line 337 is corrected there** — this ticket's AC-7 was non-closing here precisely because the corpus is a symlink no Engine-side edit can reach.
- **`neo-agent-skills#29`** — the `pr-body` job in `reusable-pr-baseline.yml`, carrying the live-body-fetch property (#17431) and, added today, the property that the body never reaches a shell `run:` block. That one existed only on PR #17917 and would otherwise have been dropped by the supersession.
- **`neo-agent-skills#14`** — the Engine's `uses:` coordinate, with the other consumers.
- **`neo-agent-skills#24`** — the AC-Evidence content check and the stacked-PR guard, both Brain-only.

**Honest residual:** the Engine is ungated until `#29` lands and `#14` wires the caller. PR #17917 would have closed that tonight; I closed it anyway rather than build a third interim duplicate, and the exposure is the argument for landing `#29` fast. Full property-transfer receipt on PR #17917.
